stories.title: Mondelez and Accenture partner on AI order processing
stories.summary: Mondelez and Accenture are collaborating to incorporate agentic AI into the order-to-cash process. The transformation aims to simplify operations, reimagine customer experience and accelerate payment collections. The approach is designed to be extensible across other business functions. The project is currently in the transformation phase.

stories.summary: - Accenture (NYSE:ACN) and Mondelēz International announced a new partnership to redesign the end-to-end Order-to-Cash process using agentic AI. - The project focuses on streamlining complex workflows across ordering, invoicing and collections for Mondelēz International's global consumer packaged goods operations. - Accenture plans to apply

stories.title: Accenture blames human error for fake AI citations
stories.summary: GPTZero identified 31 hallucinated citations in three papers linked to Accenture. The consultancy attributed errors in one agriculture report to human error, stating it found no evidence that AI caused them. The firm did not address the other two papers in its response. Human error is persistent.

stories.title: KPMG Australia government contract ban extended
stories.summary: KPMG Australia will remain excluded from new Commonwealth government contracts until 28 February 2027. The extension follows an independent review that identified serious weaknesses in the firm's ethical culture and handling of whistleblower allegations. The firm's response to internal concerns was described as poorly coordinated.

stories.title: Accenture CIO survey highlights AI execution gaps
stories.summary: Accenture's CIO Pulse survey finds enterprise AI deployment is advancing faster than measurable business returns. Governance, workforce adoption and data readiness remain obstacles to scaling. The research suggests that deliberate sequencing of workflows is the path toward stronger returns. Execution is proving to be a separate discipline.

stories.title: SEC approves audit quality rules backed by Big Four
stories.summary: The SEC has approved amendments to PCAOB quality-control standards, adopting requirements supported by Deloitte, PwC, EY and KPMG. The firms argued that original rules imposed unnecessary costs and complexity. The new standard governs how accounting firms design and evaluate their internal systems. Quality is now more flexible.

stories.title: Could Audit Firms Be Improving Their Metrics While Losing Professional Judgement?
stories.summary: Patrick Rose is a sessional academic at Griffith University in Australia, whose academic work involves digital forensics and cybersecurity investigation. stories.title: Air pollution linked to two million deaths in India
stories.summary: A report by FICCI and EY states that air pollution was attributable to over two million deaths in India in 2023. The study highlights the health consequences of fine particulate matter, which can penetrate lungs and bloodstreams. The findings link prolonged exposure to chronic respiratory and heart illnesses.

stories.title: Air pollution costs India 9.5 percent of GDP
stories.summary: A joint report by FICCI and EY estimates that air pollution costs India up to 9.5 percent of its GDP annually. The economic losses stem from declining worker productivity, rising healthcare expenditure and premature deaths. Annual business losses are estimated at 95 billion dollars, or 3 percent of GDP.

stories.title: EY reports uneven AI gains in customer service
stories.summary: EY India reports that top-performing companies saw over 50 percent improvements in customer service metrics using AI. However, the firm notes that gains remain uneven across industries. Only 23 percent of surveyed companies achieved these high-value results. Transformation is apparently not a uniform experience.

stories.title: AI value remains elusive for most
stories.summary: Only 23 percent of organizations realize high or very high value from AI in customer service, according to an EY India report. While adoption is widespread, top performers report 50 percent improvements in core metrics. For the remaining 77 percent, the transformation is still in progress.

stories.summary: AI delivers over 50% improvement in customer service KPIs for top-performing firms: EY report Only 23% of organisations have managed to realise high or very high value from artificial intelligence (AI) in customer service, even as adoption of the technology becomes widespread across businesses. stories.title: McKinsey survey finds threat incidents are common
stories.summary: Around 87 percent of organizations experienced at least one threat-related incident in the 24 months preceding a McKinsey survey. Technology infrastructure was the most affected area, with 75 percent of respondents reporting incidents. Many firms remain inadequately prepared to deal with risks beyond conventional cybersecurity.

stories.title: India faces shipbuilding output gap
stories.summary: India accounted for 0.075 percent of global merchant ship deliveries in 2025, according to a FICCI-EY report. The country delivered 57,637 gross tonnes, while Vietnam produced 15 times that amount. India currently ranks 15th among shipbuilding nations, needing an 11-fold jump to match global leaders.

stories.title: Heat stress rises as cooling access lags
stories.summary: Around 60 percent of India's population lives in areas experiencing heat stress, yet air-conditioning coverage is approximately 10 percent. McKinsey findings show that while only 4 percent of the US population faces similar heat stress, over 90 percent have access to cooling. Resources remain unevenly distributed.

stories.title: Climate adaptation needs innovation to scale
stories.summary: Global annual spending on climate adaptation could reach 1.2 trillion dollars by 2050, but 60 percent of projects are not currently deployment-ready due to financing barriers. McKinsey estimates that technological and financial innovation could make 440 billion dollars of these measures commercially viable. The challenge remains expensive.

stories.title: MNP expands with Schwartz and Company acquisition
stories.summary: Mid-market accounting firm MNP has agreed to acquire Scarborough-based Schwartz and Company. The boutique firm provides accounting and tax services to small- and medium-sized businesses. Leaders Vince Chiofalo and Gus Yantsis will join MNP as partners when the deal closes on December 1.

stories.title: EisnerAmper buys RSM Sage Intacct practice
stories.summary: EisnerAmper has acquired the Sage Intacct consulting practice from RSM US. The deal, which closes in early 2027, adds more than 35 professionals to the firm. The team specializes in implementing the financial management platform for small- and mid-sized organizations. Growth is being scaled.

stories.title: Vertex acquires Quartz Project Services
stories.summary: The Vertex Companies has acquired London-based Quartz Project Services to expand its advisory operations into Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. The deal adds construction and property consulting expertise to Vertex's existing dispute resolution and project management services. Financial terms were not disclosed.

stories.title: Asper.ai acquires Pricing One assets
stories.summary: Asper.ai has acquired key assets and talent from Geneva-based strategy firm Pricing One. The deal combines agentic AI capabilities with 650 commercial execution plans to help consumer goods companies unlock 6 to 8 percent incremental growth. The platform is expanding its presence in Europe.

stories.title: Qflow Group acquires J P Chick and Partners
stories.summary: Qflow Group has acquired engineering consultancy J P Chick and Partners, adding 35 employees and three offices to its UK platform. Qflow reports 2,500 million SEK in revenue across 41 group companies. The acquisition price for the regional consultancy was not disclosed.

stories.title: LEO Pharma to acquire dersimelagon rights
stories.summary: LEO Pharma has agreed to acquire the rights to dersimelagon from Bain-owned Tanabe for 435 million dollars. The company, which describes itself as a global leader in medical dermatology, serves nearly 100 million patients annually across 70 countries.

stories.title: JLL acquires data centre consultancy VIPA Digital
stories.summary: JLL has acquired London-based VIPA Digital for an undisclosed sum. The deal allows the commercial property adviser to offer services across the full data centre lifecycle. JLL projects infrastructure spending will reach 6.7 trillion dollars through 2030, with capacity demand expected to grow 3.5 times.

stories.title: Bridge Data Centres appoints co-CEO
stories.summary: Bridge Data Centres has appointed Drew Chen as co-CEO, effective November 1. Chen will work alongside Eric Fan to accelerate growth across the Asia Pacific region. The company cites surging cloud adoption and the rapid expansion of AI workloads as drivers for the move.

stories.title: Accenture wins Treasury financial management contract
stories.summary: Accenture Federal Services has been awarded a 10-year, 988 million dollar contract to deliver financial management solutions to the Department of the Treasury. The firm beat out four other bidders to provide cloud, data, and AI services to the Bureau of the Fiscal Service.

stories.title: Ipsum acquires B and S Group
stories.summary: Utilities business Ipsum Group has acquired Chester-based B and S Group to strengthen its Power division. The deal adds in-house manufacturing and custom electrical engineering to Ipsum's existing infrastructure services. This is the latest in a series of acquisitions for the firm during 2026.

stories.title: North Highland adds Bluestock Advisors team
stories.summary: Management consulting firm North Highland has added the 16-person team from Bluestock Advisors. Founder Jennifer Merritt will rejoin the firm as a senior managing director and Atlanta market lead. Merritt previously spent 12 years at North Highland before starting her own consultancy in 2020.

stories.title: Modi directs NITI Aayog to conduct ground-level reality checks
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has asked the NITI Aayog leadership to develop transformative ideas to improve the ease of living for marginalised people. He urged officials to collaborate with research institutions and state governments, and to personally conduct reality checks on the ground to assess actual conditions.

stories.title: Bain Capital sees hybrid capital as a partnership solution
stories.summary: Sarit Chopra, head of special situations at Bain Capital, says the firm offers hybrid capital as a partnership tool rather than a band-aid solution. The firm provides flexible capital structures, including debt and equity, to align with the next phase of business transformation for entrepreneurs seeking growth.

stories.title: ASSOCHAM calls for grid and battery investment
stories.summary: ASSOCHAM says India must strengthen its electricity grid and expand battery storage to meet climate goals. While the industry body noted progress in non-fossil fuel capacity, it warned that greater investment in supporting infrastructure is essential to ensure clean energy remains commercially viable and reliably connected.

stories.title: Cabinet approves INR 14,500 crore energy storage funding
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved a Viability Gap Funding scheme worth INR 14,500 crore to support 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage. The initiative aims to integrate renewable energy into the national network between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31, covering both battery systems and pumped hydro projects.

stories.title: EY and FICCI propose 10-year shipbuilding pipeline
stories.summary: A report by EY and FICCI recommends a 10-year vessel procurement pipeline to improve demand visibility and boost domestic shipbuilding. The authors argue that a national maritime roadmap is necessary to scale up industrial capacity and strengthen supply chains in a sector where India currently holds limited share.

stories.title: Cabinet approves critical mineral processing scheme
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved a Rs 2,814 crore capital support scheme to boost domestic processing of critical minerals like lithium and nickel. The initiative aims to reduce reliance on foreign supply chains for essential components used in electric vehicles, batteries, and defence equipment.

stories.title: Growth strategy requires economic security lens
stories.summary: As India pursues its Viksit Bharat ambitions, policy experts suggest that growth strategies must account for economic security. The focus on GDP expansion and manufacturing capabilities should be balanced with efforts to mitigate risks from illicit trade, counterfeiting, and supply chain vulnerabilities to ensure long-term resilience.

stories.title: Report highlights shipbuilding sector challenges
stories.summary: An EY and FICCI report notes that India accounted for approximately 0.075 percent of global delivered shipbuilding tonnage in 2025. The study suggests that a predictable, long-term demand pipeline and better access to financing are required to improve the sector's performance beyond its current limited market share.

stories.title: NITI Aayog study links development and net zero goals
stories.summary: A study by NITI Aayog suggests that achieving Viksit Bharat by 2047 is compatible with reaching Net Zero emissions by 2070. The report outlines a pathway for India to balance its long-term economic development goals with its international climate commitments.

stories.title: Central bank eases export reporting for small services
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has simplified reporting rules for small-value service exports. Resident individuals will be deemed to have submitted required declarations upon providing payment information to their banks, while non-individual exporters receive similar treatment for receipts up to INR 1 million.

stories.title: Water availability emerges as industrial constraint
stories.summary: As India pushes for more factories and data centres, water scarcity is becoming a significant business constraint. Industry observers note that while water will not stop national growth, it will determine which specific industrial clusters succeed and at what cost to the surrounding environment.

stories.title: Accenture manager highlights human side of data careers
stories.summary: Kate Wallace, an AI and data senior manager at Accenture, says her career path was shaped by a blend of technical statistics and interpersonal relationships. She argues that the human element of building connections remains a vital part of data science work.

stories.title: Harvard FAS expects to recover McKinsey costs
stories.summary: The Faculty of Arts and Sciences expects to recoup its spending on McKinsey & Company in less than six months. The firm was hired to advise on a staff restructuring that eliminated roughly 150 positions, a move now estimated to save the school $18.5 million annually.

stories.title: Harvard FAS declines to disclose McKinsey fees
stories.summary: The Faculty of Arts and Sciences says it will recoup its spending on McKinsey & Company in under six months following a staff restructuring. While the school confirmed the consultants advised on the changes, it declined to disclose the total cost of the engagement.

stories.title: Book explores human judgment in AI-driven consulting
stories.summary: A new book by a former McKinsey consultant, Gaurav Bhosle, argues that AI cannot replace the judgment and self-awareness required in consulting. The bestseller suggests that the human side of the profession remains the most critical component as firms increasingly integrate automated tools into their workflows.

stories.title: MBA student details consulting recruitment
stories.summary: Elliott T. Raia, co-chair of the Management Consulting Group at Booth, says there is a high probability that someone with a similar background has already successfully recruited for consulting. He notes the group provides support throughout the MBA journey. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: McKinsey appoints Bolanle Asumah as director of people
stories.summary: Bolanle Asumah has been appointed as director of people in the Middle East for McKinsey. A human resource leader with 20 years of experience, Asumah previously worked at KPMG for 9 years. She says her passion is helping people and organisations realise their full potential.

stories.title: Appliers.ai acquires consultancy Prevail
stories.summary: Melbourne-based AI specialist Appliers.ai has acquired consultancy Prevail to deepen its enterprise capabilities. Prevail co-founder Pete Gatt joins as chief technology officer, while Ben Ashby becomes chief solutions officer. Financial terms were not disclosed. The AI market continues to consolidate as demand for transformation accelerates.

stories.title: Adastra forms global executive team
stories.summary: Adastra has announced a seven-person global executive team to guide the firm through its next phase of growth. Backed by private equity firm Carlyle, the data and AI consulting company employs 2,200 professionals. The firm plans to combine organic expansion with selective acquisitions to grow.

stories.title: Access denied to MBA college list
stories.summary: The requested information regarding MBA colleges in India with low fees and good placements is currently unavailable. The server returned an access denied error. The page remains unreachable. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Uzzi and Lall appoints Rajiv Chandak to lead India operations
stories.summary: Uzzi and Lall has appointed Rajiv Chandak as managing director and head of India. The announcement follows the firm's ongoing leadership changes. The full details of the appointment are currently unavailable due to site access restrictions.
